templates_considered: LOG-001 (no_sensitive_data_in_logs): fits the 'cardholder can't be logged' part; used as is
VND-001 (approved_vendors_only): fits the 'Stripe and Plaid only' part; used with hosts only
CONF-011 (sensitive_fields_marked): checks a field IS marked sensitive, not that a field is absent; does not express 'not stored raw'; not used
CONF-012 (confidential_tables_tagged): tags tables, does not forbid storage; not used
DATA-010 (no_pii_in_responses): about what endpoints fetch/return, not storage or logs; not used
SEC-012 (no_secrets_in_code): fits the twilio token literal found in acme_notify_sms, outside the ask; not written, proposed in reply
CONF-010 (sensitive_tables_need_login): relevant to payments access but not asked; not used

rules.covers: cardholder data must not be logged (debug.log only)
only Stripe and Plaid as recipients; kinds, providers left empty so cloud, email and agent.llm providers are all reported
cardholder and bank data must not be stored raw (field-name based)

ask_parts_not_covered.part: cardholder data must not be logged via datadog.log or other log sinks
data is not stored raw (encryption cannot be verified; card data under other field names is missed)
PCI audit pass as a whole (controls, access reviews, network scope, process)
cardholder data must not be sent to a vendor not on the list, beyond host names (data inside an approved vendor's call is not inspected)

assumptions: The approved vendor hosts are api.stripe.com and production.plaid.com, the two in use in the workspace
'Stored raw' means the field exists in a table with the name listed; the customer's field names match the workspace's
cardholder_name and bank fields are in scope for 'cardholder stuff'
Advisory enforcement is the right default; the customer did not specify blocking
Policy tag 'pci-dss' is an acceptable label; no specific PCI DSS requirement number was recorded
confusions: outbound.vendor_allowlist: providers and hosts both 'empty means unreviewed'; not obvious whether omitting providers flags Stripe/Plaid under a cloud provider id, so I relied on hosts only

table.field_attribute_required: 'forbidden' with attribute unset is described as reporting every selected field, but the field-selection-plus-attribute semantics are spread across the description; I had to infer that attribute can stay empty
No check forbids a field by name with a pattern (e.g. any field matching card or pan); had to enumerate names, which is weaker
Template LOG-001 says add datadog.log for full coverage, but gives no datadog.log rule example; unclear whether to add it as a second rule
Policy tags: no guidance on whether tags should record framework criteria such as PCI DSS requirement numbers
wished_for: A check or param to forbid fields matching a name pattern (card*, *_cvv) across all tables
A template or recipe for 'data must not be stored' distinct from 'marked sensitive'
Guidance on vendor allowlists when a vendor is reached through a provider id versus a host
A PCI DSS or framework-to-check mapping in the catalogue
why_confidence: The logging and vendor rules match the ask and use template checks, and all three files parse cleanly. Storage is checked by field name only, so renamed or differently-named card fields would be missed. The policies were not evaluated, so I have no run result, and a PCI audit pass depends on controls outside any policy.
